items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-09-30
items.q: I played with the band... Thomas Benton, he's on the guitar... Tommy would be on the piano... And I'd be out then.

ctx.x: When you were working for Billy Phillips, were you playing with the band or along?

Yeah. I played with the band. And this is what used to happen. I'm playing piano with the band. Now, first, he's leading violin. He's on his violin. I'm playing the piano. Thomas Benton, he's on the guitar. And sometimes be like that. Now sometimes it change around. And Tommy would be on the piano. See? And I'd be out then. So let's just change the minutes. And hands around. Tom lived up here in the garden. I did too. See? I lived up here on the drive to the second and third at the time. And Thomas lived a little…
What about Big Cornie? Did you ever work with him?

items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-07-01
items.q: I played with him once. We both. I was in the band he was playing in.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah, yeah. He's good. Who did he play with? Your man? Yeah, I played with him once. We both. I was in the band he was playing in. What did he used to do? I said, how did he used to do? You see? He used to find musicians so fast in that day. Find high on some days. Well then, it's like you didn't follow you talk about the this man is still the leader. I might say. jack. He's been dead. His sister's living now, Thomas Benton's sister. Is she in his neighborhood? Yeah. She lives at, let me see, she lives 3924 Magnolia Street now. 3924 Magnolia? Yeah, Thomas Benton's sister. I was talking to her yesterday. And she's glad to see me. She hadn't seen me in 50 years until yesterday. Oh she's up near Dave Bailey. You know Dave Bailey, a drummer. Yeah, she hadn't seen me 50 years until yesterday. And she told me to come see us sometime. And I just played her brother years ago.…

items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-07-01
